text.p: Bonds were at record highs in thin early trade, bathing in the warm glow of European Union approval for Portugal's convergence plan.
Traders said the key 10-year benchmark cash could narrow the yield gap with the Bund towards 75 basis points, breaking below the previous floor of 80.
A slightly firmer escudo against the mark, with the currency trading at 100.64/67 against its closing 100.73/78, was also helping the tone.
"Cash (bond) prices could rise, with the 10-years touching 75 basis points to the Bund today if Spain gains and the escudo remains free of pressure," said one broker.
"There is also the help coming from expectations for a very good inflation number in April," he said.
The market was waiting for the results of the Credit Institute's three-year bond auction which could result in yields below secondary market levels.
Traders saw bids at between 5.45 and 5.55 percent with some saying the Institute will not accept anything above 5.50 percent. --Sergio Goncalves, Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
